item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-ef08c2a2e0160331","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In 2023, the UN system supported the federal government’s response to the Yanomami crisis through 13 UN entities, covering nutrition, health, environment, water and sanitation, human rights, crime prevention, and productive inclusion.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.6","6B.9","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 government response.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes cooperation with the federal government during Lula’s presidency, but does not attribute every implementation result personally to Lula.","limitations":["UN-reported support and activities do not independently establish final outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ef08c2a2e0160331","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The UN system signed and began implementing the 2023–2027 Cooperation Framework with Brazil and partnered with IPEA to strengthen monitoring of Sustainable Development Goal implementation.","question_ids":["6B.5","6B.9","8B.2","8B.5"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns institutional actions initiated in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies alignment and cooperation with the federal government; it does not establish Lula’s individual direction.","limitations":["The source does not provide budget execution or measured welfare outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ef08c2a2e0160331","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The UN system launched the Brazil-UN Fund for Sustainable Amazon Development, focused on sustainable economic inclusion for vulnerable people in the region.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","6B.3","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns a 2023 institutional initiative.","ruler_attribution":"The initiative was launched in cooperation with Brazil, but the source does not attribute the decision solely to Lula.","limitations":["No disbursed amount or beneficiary outcome is reported."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"After the January 8 attacks on Congress, the Supreme Court, and the presidential palace, police arrested about 1,500 people; prosecutors had charged about 1,300 by October, and 25 had been convicted by mid-November.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.4","4B.10","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns a 2023 domestic constitutional crisis.","ruler_attribution":"The figures concern state enforcement during Lula’s presidency, but arrests were ordered by a Supreme Court justice rather than shown as personally directed by Lula.","limitations":["The source does not assess proportionality or due-process quality of all cases."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The Lula administration reversed selected Bolsonaro-era environmental and sexual-reproductive-rights policies but did not take decisive measures to address chronic police abuse.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.5","3B.10","4B.10","8B.8","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly evaluates the administration during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the policy reversals and failure to address police abuse to the Lula administration.","limitations":["The assessment is qualitative and does not specify every reversed policy or define decisive action."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The federal government conditioned transfers of public-security funds to states on reductions in police killings and other factors.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.6","3B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns a 2023 federal policy.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the funding condition to the federal government under Lula.","limitations":["The source does not report whether the condition changed state behavior or reduced killings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Police killed 28 people in São Paulo’s Baixada Santista region during an operation launched after a military police officer was killed; Human Rights Watch identified significant investigative gaps, including deficient forensic analysis.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns a July–September 2023 operation.","ruler_attribution":"The operation was conducted by São Paulo police; the source does not establish Lula’s direct operational control, while federal policy oversight is not specified.","limitations":["The evidence concerns subnational authorities and does not establish federal authorization."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Gender-based violence increased in the first half of 2023: 34,000 rapes of women and girls were reported, up 15 percent from the same period in 2022, and killings of women rose 2.6 percent to 1,902.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The figures describe conditions during Lula’s presidency but do not establish presidential causation.","limitations":["The source does not isolate federal policy effects or reporting changes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Congress approved laws requiring specialized women’s police stations to remain open 24/7 and guaranteeing equal pay for women and men doing the same jobs; the ILO Violence and Harassment Convention had not been ratified by November.","question_ids":["3B.7","5B.8","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns legislative activity during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The laws were approved during Lula’s presidency, but the source does not state that Lula proposed or controlled their passage; non-ratification remained unresolved.","limitations":["Enactment is documented, but implementation and enforcement are not."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In January, the Lula administration revoked a 2020 rule requiring health professionals to report rape survivors seeking abortion.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.7","4B.10","8B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns a January 2023 executive action.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch directly attributes the revocation to the Lula administration.","limitations":["The source does not measure subsequent access to lawful abortion services."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The government appointed the first Indigenous leaders to chair Brazil’s Indigenous affairs agency and the newly created Ministry of Indigenous Peoples.","question_ids":["4B.5","4B.7","6B.3","6B.4","8B.4"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 appointments.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the appointments to the Lula administration.","limitations":["The source does not assess appointee performance or institutional resources."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The Lula administration withdrew a Bolsonaro-era bill allowing mining and other commercial activities in Indigenous territories, revoked policies facilitating encroachment, and resumed titling of Indigenous lands.","question_ids":["4B.7","5B.4","6B.3","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 executive policy changes.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch directly attributes these actions to the Lula administration.","limitations":["Congress later enacted legislation contrary to a Supreme Court ruling on Indigenous land rights."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"In response to documented malnutrition and serious disease linked to illegal mining in Yanomami territory, the government launched a large-scale operation to remove thousands of miners; Yanomami associations later reported continuing health problems and the return of some miners.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.6","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns actions and outcomes during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the emergency operation to the Lula government.","limitations":["The source reports partial persistence of the problem and does not quantify operational resources or long-term effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"From January through October 2023, 4,776 square kilometers of Amazon rainforest were cleared, a 49 percent decrease from the same period in 2022, while 6,802 square kilometers of Cerrado were deforested, a 34 percent increase.","question_ids":["1B.9","5B.1","5B.6","6B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 environmental outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The outcomes occurred during Lula’s presidency; the source links them to policy context but does not establish sole presidential causation.","limitations":["The comparison is year-over-year and does not establish the full causal contribution of federal policy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The government updated its climate plan with targets to cut emissions 48 percent by 2025 and 53 percent by 2030 and renewed its commitment to zero illegal Amazon deforestation by 2030, while also announcing fossil-fuel investments and observer participation in OPEC+ despite its ecological-transition rhetoric.","question_ids":["1B.9","5B.1","5B.3","8B.1","8B.2","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 climate commitments and policy choices.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes the updated plan, deforestation commitment, fossil-fuel investments, and OPEC+ decision to the Lula administration.","limitations":["The source does not evaluate implementation of the targets by year-end."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Lula offered to broker Russia-Ukraine peace talks but made statements incorrectly suggesting Kyiv and Moscow were equally responsible for starting the war.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.3","2B.7","7B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns Lula’s 2023 foreign-policy conduct.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch directly attributes both the peace-brokering offer and the statement to Lula.","limitations":["The source does not report whether the proposal produced negotiations or changed the conflict."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b923505f0b609e23","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Brazil declined in March to sign a Human Rights Council declaration condemning abuses in Nicaragua, later expressed extreme concern about Nicaraguan violations and offered to receive stripped political refugees, and continued declining statements concerning China’s abuses against Uyghurs.","question_ids":["2B.6","2B.9","7B.1","7B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 diplomatic positions.","ruler_attribution":"Human Rights Watch attributes these positions to Brazil under Lula’s government.","limitations":["The source does not explain the government’s stated rationale for each position."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd52bc1c2df98cdb","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The government’s human-rights ombudsman received more than 3.4 million complaints in 2023, including racism, physical and psychological violence, and sexual harassment, a 41 percent increase from the previous year.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.6","3B.7","6B.5","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports a 2023 institutional indicator.","ruler_attribution":"The complaints were recorded by a state body during Lula’s presidency; the increase does not by itself establish increased underlying abuse or presidential causation.","limitations":["Complaint volume may reflect reporting or access changes, not only incidence."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd52bc1c2df98cdb","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Bolsa Família supported 21.4 million families in 2023, and government data indicated that 3 million beneficiary families moved above the poverty line between March and September.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.8","5B.9","6B.2","6B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 program reach and reported results.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the program and government data to Brazil during Lula’s administration.","limitations":["The source does not provide a counterfactual or independently verify the attribution of poverty exits."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd52bc1c2df98cdb","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In 2023, more than 70 million people experienced food insecurity and 21.1 million, or 10 percent of the population, experienced hunger; the Brasil Sem Fome plan targeted a 2.5 percent poverty reduction and removal from the FAO hunger map by 2030.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.8","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","6B.6","8B.1","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 conditions and a government plan.","ruler_attribution":"The plan is attributed to the Brazilian government under Lula; the food-insecurity figures describe national conditions without presidential causation.","limitations":["The plan’s 2030 targets were not yet outcomes in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd52bc1c2df98cdb","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The unemployment rate fell from 9.2 percent in 2022 to 7.7 percent in the third quarter of 2023, while 39 million people remained employed in the informal sector.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 labor-market outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The figures describe Brazil during Lula’s presidency but do not establish that Lula’s policies caused the change.","limitations":["The informal-sector figure indicates persistent employment-quality and protection problems."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd52bc1c2df98cdb","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"UNICEF data indicated that 2 million Brazilian children and adolescents, 10 percent of the total, were not attending school in 2023; child labor accounted for 48 percent of stated reasons and learning difficulties for 30 percent.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 education access.","ruler_attribution":"The figures concern Brazil during Lula’s presidency but do not establish federal causation.","limitations":["The source does not identify which level of government was responsible for the shortfall."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd52bc1c2df98cdb","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Between July and September 2023, at least 394 people were killed in police operations in Bahia, Rio de Janeiro, and São Paulo; Amnesty reported that a 2019 Supreme Court order to reduce police violence continued to be disregarded.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 police violence and compliance failures.","ruler_attribution":"The killings were by state police and the order was directed principally at public authorities; the source does not establish Lula’s direct command responsibility.","limitations":["The figures cover three states and do not represent all national police killings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd52bc1c2df98cdb","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"In São Paulo’s Baixada Santista operation beginning July 28, police arrested 958 people and killed 30; Amnesty documented 11 serious human-rights violations, including extrajudicial executions, unlawful home entry, torture, and other ill-treatment.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns a 2023 operation.","ruler_attribution":"The operation was conducted by São Paulo security forces; the source does not establish Lula’s direct operational control.","limitations":["The documented violations are attributed to Amnesty’s investigation and do not establish final judicial findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd52bc1c2df98cdb","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The government approved demarcation of eight Indigenous territories in 2023, but 134 territories remained only at the initial examination stage; Congress overrode Lula’s veto of major provisions limiting demarcation.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.7","6B.3","8B.2","8B.5","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 Indigenous-land decisions and institutional resistance.","ruler_attribution":"Amnesty attributes the approval and veto to Lula’s government and the override to Congress.","limitations":["The source does not identify the size or status of each approved territory."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bd52bc1c2df98cdb","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The government had not ratified the Escazú Agreement in 2023, and Climate Action Tracker judged climate-adaptation and mitigation measures highly insufficient, citing inadequate planning and federal coordination.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.9","6B.6","8B.2","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 environmental governance.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment concerns the federal government under Lula.","limitations":["Climate Action Tracker’s assessment is an external evaluation and the source does not detail all measures reviewed."]},{"source_id":"SRC-28c47ca8396885ee","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"CIMI characterized Lula’s first year as marked by renewed monitoring and some suppression of invaders, but insufficient demarcation, protection, and assistance; Congress weakened the Indigenous Peoples Ministry and enacted Law 14.701 after overriding Lula’s partial veto.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.7","6B.3","8B.2","8B.5","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly evaluates 2023 Indigenous policy.","ruler_attribution":"CIMI attributes the renewed federal actions and partial veto to Lula’s government, while attributing contrary legislation to Congress.","limitations":["CIMI is an advocacy organization and the summary does not provide independent verification for every assessment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-28c47ca8396885ee","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"CIMI recorded 276 cases of illegal resource exploitation or property damage across at least 202 Indigenous territories in 22 states in 2023, while only eight Indigenous Lands were homologated.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 institutional and territorial outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The outcomes occurred during Lula’s administration; CIMI describes federal operations but does not establish sole presidential causation.","limitations":["The report’s case counts are not equivalent to a complete national administrative register."]},{"source_id":"SRC-28c47ca8396885ee","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"CIMI recorded 1,040 deaths of Indigenous children aged 0–4 in 2023, including deaths from pneumonia, diarrhea, and malnutrition, and recorded 111 deaths attributed to lack of healthcare.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports 2023 Indigenous child-health outcomes.","ruler_attribution":"The figures concern conditions during Lula’s presidency; CIMI attributes categories to state omission but not personal presidential direction.","limitations":["The source notes that monitoring categories and data collection changed, affecting comparison with prior years."]},{"source_id":"SRC-28c47ca8396885ee","start_unit":7,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The new administration renewed restriction ordinances for isolated Indigenous groups, but at least 56 of 119 recorded groups were in territories invaded in 2023, and operations were generally insufficient to guarantee effective protection.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.3","8B.2","8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 protective measures and remaining exposure.","ruler_attribution":"CIMI attributes renewal of the ordinances to the new federal administration under Lula.","limitations":["The source does not quantify the personnel or funding devoted to each operation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b00971cd0dd72536","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"UNICEF reported that multidimensional poverty among Brazilian children and adolescents fell from 34.3 million, or 62.5 percent, in 2017 to 28.8 million, or 55.9 percent, in 2023; extreme multidimensional poverty fell from 13 million to 9.8 million.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly reports the 2023 endpoint of a 2017–2023 series.","ruler_attribution":"UNICEF says the reduction was influenced mainly by increased income, especially expanded Bolsa Família, and improved information access; it does not attribute the entire change solely to Lula.","limitations":["The report was published in 2025 and the comparison does not isolate changes occurring specifically during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98d18485e241f096","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The US State Department reported numerous unlawful or arbitrary killings by state police in 2023 and said the government did not always take credible steps to identify and punish officials responsible for abuses; 39 percent of a 2011–2021 sample of police-homicide investigations resulted in indictments.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The killings and government assessment concern 2023; the investigation statistic is historical context.","ruler_attribution":"The report assesses the Brazilian government and state police during Lula’s presidency but does not establish personal presidential direction.","limitations":["The indictment statistic covers 2011–2021 rather than 2023 alone."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98d18485e241f096","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The State Department reported that freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, association, internet access, and independent monitoring generally operated without federal restriction in 2023, and that press freedom improved after Bolsonaro’s departure, although threats, criminal defamation rules, and online violence remained.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the institutional environment in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes government practice during Lula’s presidency and attributes improved press freedom partly to Bolsonaro’s departure, not specifically to Lula’s reforms.","limitations":["The report also records legal and nonstate constraints that continued."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98d18485e241f096","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The government continued voluntarily relocating Venezuelan refugees and asylum seekers from northern border states; more than 100,000 people had been relocated to other states to reduce pressure on Roraima and improve access to education and work.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns government implementation reported in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The State Department attributes the relocation process to the Brazilian government.","limitations":["The source does not identify Lula’s personal role or report outcomes after relocation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98d18485e241f096","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"In 2023 Lula announced measures including equal-pay policy, free sanitary-pad distribution, 270 vehicles for Maria da Penha patrols, an 8 percent federal workforce quota for women survivors of violence, and recognition of Marielle Franco Day; the equal-pay law was not yet enforced.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","5B.8","6B.3","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns measures announced or enacted in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The State Department directly attributes the measures to President Lula and the federal government.","limitations":["Several measures were announcements or laws whose implementation was incomplete."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98d18485e241f096","start_unit":10,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"Lula established Brazil’s first Ministry of Indigenous Peoples, re-established the National Council for Indigenous Policy, and restructured the National Foundation of Indigenous Peoples.","question_ids":["4B.5","4B.7","6B.3","6B.9","8B.2","8B.4"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 institutional creation and restructuring.","ruler_attribution":"The State Department directly attributes these actions to President Lula and his government.","limitations":["The source does not assess staffing, budget execution, or performance of the new institutions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-98d18485e241f096","start_unit":12,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"The federal government created a national council for LGBTQI+ rights, restored after its predecessor was eliminated under Bolsonaro, and standardized use of social names in federal administration; violence and discrimination against LGBTQI+ people nevertheless remained substantial.","question_ids":["3B.7","4B.7","6B.8","6B.9","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023 institutional measures and conditions.","ruler_attribution":"The State Department attributes the council’s creation and social-name decree to the federal government under Lula.","limitations":["The source does not establish the council’s operational results by year-end."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-3e8fded6ffbe2dae","SRC-6455cd1695e4aa49","SRC-d6d99ef20664c818","SRC-0548e24cc641f199","SRC-e82e02a2210db6ad","SRC-c7ce9ceab60e68a3"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents primarily covered 2022, provided only bibliographic or global material, or did not contain concrete Lula-period facts specific to 2023.","Facts concerning state governments, Congress, courts, NGOs, or international organizations are included where they materially illuminate Lula’s authority, policies, institutional constraints, or outcomes, but are not treated as proof of personal presidential control.","No scores or overall chapter judgments are provided."]}
